name: put the eye where the drawing straightens out
one_line: A drawing stretched so that it is right from one point and nowhere else, and eleven rungs that are one width seen from there.
how: Mark a cross on the short edge of an A4; every distance is measured from it. Print eleven horizontal bars centred on the middle of the sheet, each a quarter as long as its distance from the cross — the nearest 30 mm long at 120 mm, the furthest 60 mm long at 240 mm, the gaps widening as they go. From above it is a crooked ladder. Then: sheet flat on the table, chin over the cross, eye lowered to 4 cm from the paper, looking along it. From there the rungs are one width and evenly spaced, and half a centimetre higher they are not. Then ask for one of their own: any drawing 2 cm tall, cut into ten rows, each row carried out to the printed distances.

knobs.knob: how high the eye is held
knobs.effect: four centimetres above the paper with the first bar at 120 mm makes 23.8 mm the tallest straight picture that fits on an A4; lower and the sheet needed runs off towards infinity, higher and the stretch is too mild to surprise.

knobs.knob: whether the viewpoint is an eye or a camera
knobs.effect: with an eye at the mark the effect lives in the room and a photograph of the sheet destroys it, since the camera records the smear. With a camera and two real things at the same height-over-distance ratio, the photograph is the only place it exists.
a printed cross hands over the answer and leaves only the looking; no mark makes finding the point the exercise, and on a stretch this steep it is found by trial in about a minute.

copying eleven numbers teaches nothing about why they are those numbers; carrying a small drawing of their own out to the same distances is the only part that comes back on a sheet and can be checked.

where_the_work_is: In the ratio between each bar's length and its distance from the cross, which is constant and is the whole construction. A bar 2 mm wrong is invisible from above, where everything is a smear, and unmissable from the mark.
breaks: The eye cannot be scaled and the sheet can. Everything is set against an eye 4 cm above the paper, so a page printed at 94% to fit the margins puts the viewpoint where no chin goes, the rungs never line up, and nothing says why. Print at 100% and check that the first bar sits 120 mm from the cross. A photograph of the finished sheet carries none of it, because the effect is not in the plane photographed; what comes back is the reader's own construction. None of it exists on a display, which is flat and already in front of the eye.
